candidates.next_evidence: Check latest ZIM 6-K/20-F, current service network, Asia-US and Middle East route exposure, emergency surcharges, spot freight indices, charter commitments, and any acquisition or regulatory status updates.
candidates.node_relation: Direct exposure to container shipping rate volatility, route disruption, and effective capacity tightening during maritime chokepoint stress.
candidates.theme_relation: If Red Sea, Hormuz, Panama Canal, or other chokepoints force longer routes, surcharges, or schedule unreliability, container liners can experience episodic pricing power, though overcapacity can reverse the benefit quickly.
candidates.why_include: ZIM is a US-listed global container liner and is directly mapped to the container freight-rate and routing disruption channel. It is useful as a high-beta candidate for chokepoint-driven freight volatility, but requires live rate and route data before any stronger conclusion.

candidates.next_evidence: Review latest fleet list, charter expirations, average remaining charter duration, liner counterparties, exposure to mid-sized vessels, and current containership charter-rate benchmarks.
candidates.node_relation: Supplier of containership capacity to liner companies; effective capacity scarcity can improve demand for leased vessels when route diversions absorb fleet capacity.
candidates.theme_relation: A diffuse congestion regime can turn vessel availability into a bottleneck, especially if longer voyages, congestion, or rerouting absorb ship-days and increase liner demand for chartered tonnage.
candidates.why_include: GSL provides containership capacity rather than freight forwarding services. That makes it a second-order capacity supplier candidate if chokepoints tighten effective fleet availability. However, contract duration, charter rates, fleet size class, and counterparty exposure must be checked.

candidates.next_evidence: Check latest Matson 10-K/10-Q for China service volumes, Hawaii/Alaska/Guam volume trends, freight-rate sensitivity, fuel surcharges, port congestion commentary, and customer demand for expedited services.
candidates.node_relation: Regional and transpacific ocean carrier/logistics operator with exposure to expedited Pacific routes and US non-contiguous domestic trade lanes.
candidates.theme_relation: Regionalized, shorter-route, or premium expedited services may become more valuable when global routes are disrupted or when importers prioritize reliability over lowest freight cost.
candidates.why_include: Matson is not a pure global chokepoint carrier, but its Pacific and domestic non-contiguous ocean transportation network can serve as a reliability and regional-route exposure candidate during global logistics disruption.

candidates.next_evidence: Track latest ocean container volumes, ocean revenue/gross profit, airfreight substitution, customs brokerage growth, management commentary on disruption, and margin impact from carrier-rate volatility.
candidates.node_relation: Asset-light global logistics provider that arranges ocean, air, customs, warehousing, distribution, and order-management services during disruptions.
candidates.theme_relation: When shippers face unreliable sailings, port congestion, rerouting, or mode substitution, freight forwarders can gain relevance as problem-solvers even if ocean volumes or pricing compress margins.
candidates.why_include: Expeditors is a major US-listed freight forwarder with explicit ocean freight and disruption-management relevance. It is less directly tied to freight-rate upside than liners, but can benefit from complexity, customs needs, and rerouting demand.

candidates.next_evidence: Verify Aon’s marine insurance revenue exposure, war-risk placement activity, client demand trends, premium commission sensitivity, and whether marine is financially material within total Aon revenue.
candidates.node_relation: Marine insurance and risk-transfer broker serving shipowners, operators, ports, terminals, logistics firms, and supply-chain companies.
candidates.theme_relation: War-risk insurance can become a regulated/financial input bottleneck in maritime crises; brokers with marine practices may see higher client demand for risk placement, analytics, and advisory services.
candidates.why_include: Insurance availability and war-risk pricing are central to whether ships can economically transit high-risk chokepoints. Aon is not a shipper, but its marine insurance practice maps to the risk-transfer layer of the chokepoint stack.

memory_update.text: Add ZIM as a direct, high-beta US-listed container liner candidate for maritime chokepoint-driven freight-rate volatility; keep evidence requirement high because container overcapacity can offset disruption benefits.
Add GSL as a containership capacity supplier candidate; the thesis depends on effective fleet scarcity, charter-rate benchmarks, and charter expiry timing rather than spot freight rates alone.
Add MATX as a regionalized and expedited Pacific ocean/logistics candidate rather than a pure global chokepoint exposure.
Add EXPD as an asset-light logistics complexity beneficiary candidate; monitor whether disruption increases solution demand enough to offset ocean-volume and pricing pressure.

Marine war-risk insurance should be treated as a regulated/financial input bottleneck in the maritime chokepoint stack; AON is a candidate for the broker/risk-transfer layer, but materiality must be verified.

Need a separate pass for non-US-listed but globally important leaders such as Maersk, Hapag-Lloyd, CMA CGM, DP World, PSA, COSCO, and major port operators; they are central to the node but outside this US-listed pass.

node: Maritime, geopolitical, and weather-driven logistics chokepoints
summary: Expanded a focused US-listed universe for the maritime chokepoint node. The strongest direct exposures are container carriers and containership capacity owners, while second-order exposures include regional ocean/logistics operators, asset-light freight forwarders, and marine insurance/risk-transfer brokers. This is a timing-sensitive node: company-level conclusions require live freight rates, vessel routing, insurance premium data, port congestion, and confirmation of each company’s trade-lane exposure.
